title: How is carrier roll compensation credited on a Container Bookings booking?
content:
## When this applies
This entry covers the Container Bookings product line. Compensation for a carrier roll is owed from the day the roll was recorded, whether or not it was credited at that time; a carrier roll whose compensation was not credited is credited when the booking is next handled.

## Business effect of the credit
Crediting adds one roll compensation entry, dated today, to the booking's charge history, pointing at the roll entry it compensates, and lowers the booking's outstanding charges by exactly the amount credited. The roll entry itself, the booking's sailing, containers and status are not touched.

## How it is invoked
The credit is made with **credit_roll_compensation_f67bce09**, an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock) and then called (call) by the agent. The tool books exactly the amount passed in; it does not compute an amount and does not check any business condition.

## Parameters
| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| booking_id | the booking reference number of the booking being credited, as returned by the booking lookup for the verified customer | identifier |
| reference_event_id | the reference number of the carrier roll entry being compensated, as shown in the booking's charge history | identifier |
| compensation_usd | the compensation to credit, in USD | a positive decimal amount with 2 decimal places; a value given with more digits is rounded half-to-even to 2 decimal places when booked |

## Return
The tool returns a text rendering of a dictionary describing the booked credit: booking_event_id (reference of the new compensation entry), booking_id (the booking credited), charge_code (always roll_compensation), reference_event_id (the roll entry compensated), amount_usd (the credit booked, USD with 2 decimal places), event_date (YYYY-MM-DD, the booking date of the entry) and charges_due_usd (the booking's outstanding charges after the credit, USD with 2 decimal places). A returned booking_event_id means the credit is on the account. The entry carries the booking's equipment type and records no container count.

## Points of judgement
**The roll happened two weeks ago and nothing was credited then. Is compensation still owed?** It has been owed since the day the roll was recorded and is credited when the booking is next handled.
